text:
leah: Quick thread — propose adding a lightweight 'shard-probe' RPC + tighter loader interface to make streaming warmup safer when shards are remote. thinking: a cheap HEAD-style call that returns shapes, byte-range map, small readiness hints, and a fast checksum so the runtime can make better prefetch/eager-warmup decisions.

michael: +1. sketch: probe should be <1KB response, no model bytes. return: num_tensors, per-tensor (offset,len), small rolling checksum, and 'hot_hint' (bool) if shard already in remote edge cache. helps avoid blind prefetch of 100s of MB.

anya: main tradeoff is added RTT for many tiny shards. if callers do N parallel probes it still hits latency. can we piggyback probe info into existing range GETs if the server supports a custom header? or do we make probe optional with heuristics (only for >X shards or >YMB)?

sam: implementation note: server-side we can expose probe via the same object-storage endpoints as an HTTP HEAD or an endpoint like /shard/<id>/probe. clients: WeightSource.resolve(shard) -> ProbeResult. loader API boundary: Resolve -> OpenStream(range[]) -> Read. Keep Resolve extremely cheap.

olga: small spec suggestion for safetensors: add an optional 8-byte footer field (safetensors-ext-probe) that contains a 64-bit farmhash + a small manifest table of (name,offset,len). currently we parse header which can be slow for compressed/packed bundles. embedding a compact probe table would let remote servers answer probe without scanning the whole file.

leah: good. also want explicit warmup policies in runtime config so we don't have carte blanche prefetch. proposal: warmup.policy = {type: "probing", threshold_mb: 16, parallel_probes: 8, eager_prefetch_ratio: 0.2}. example:

```yaml
warmup:
  policy: probing
  threshold_mb: 16
  parallel_probes: 8
  eager_prefetch_ratio: 0.15  # fraction of shard to fetch before first request
  fallback: mmap_local  # strategy if probe fails
```

michael: fallback should be deterministic: if probe fails or probe says not-hot -> do range-requests for first N bytes that cover kv-cache headers, then stream rest on demand. avoids tens of small HTTP calls during generation.

anya: can we add a quick local-cache admission: if shard < 4MB, always download fully; if > 4MB, use probe-based partial hydration. simplifies heuristics.

sam: i can draft the WeightSource API RFC: methods: resolve(shard_id) -> ProbeResult, open_ranges(shard_id, ranges[]) -> AsyncStream, close(shard_id). probe result shape: {shard_id, total_bytes, tensor_index: [(name,offset,len)], checksum64, hot_hint}. keeping it plain JSON for now.

olga: compatibility: we MUST make probe optional and backwards-compatible with existing safetensors blobs. servers that can't answer probe should return 501 -> client falls back. note to infra: S3 and GCS can serve a small sidecar manifest (/<shard>.probe) to avoid changing format.

infra-bot: deploy-check queued for probe-sidecar endpoint (infra/objstore) — ticket INF-3146.

leah: action items: 1) sam write loader-api RFC draft (owner: sam) 2) olga sketch safetensors optional probe footer and sidecar option (owner: olga) 3) michael + infra to prototype probe endpoint and perf compare (owner: michael). target: bench (<20% extra latency on cold start for big models) and reduced bytes downloaded during warmup.

anya: +1 on owners. add unit tests for probe fallback (simulate 501 and malformed probe).

leah: thanks — feel free to add specifics to the RFC draft thread. short-term we'll gate this behind a runtime flag so Dedicated customers can opt-in. :rocket:
